ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show fee in favour of the driver; no refund to the rider.
ruling.reasoning:
No-show screen: nothing in the complaint, chat or driver statement alleges threats, harassment, dangerous driving or any safety matter — safety_concern "none".

Which clause (NS-0): the driver cancelled ("cancelled_by":"driver") and his statement gives rider no-show as the reason ("After pressing I'm Here I waited more than 5 minutes at the pickup. No rider, so I cancelled."). His own words, not just the app reason, so NS-1 applies.

NS-1 conditions:
(i) Arrival — app_event driver_arrived at 18:21:55; GPS at 18:22:00 is (1.332516, 103.741448). Pickup point Jurong East MRT is (1.33218, 103.74155). Offset ≈ 37 m east–west + 0.4 m north ≈ ~37 m, well within 200 m. Met.
(ii) Free wait — arrival 18:21:55, scheduled/effective start of wait 18:21:55; cancellation 18:27:55 = exactly 6 min 0 s, which exceeds the 5-minute free wait. No record-specific threshold (no 8-min value in this record). Met.
(iii) Contact — one in-app message at 18:22:25 ("At the pickup now, grey Kia Niro.") and one in-app call at 18:23:25 (unanswered, 0 s). Requirement is ≥1 message AND ≥1 call; call need not be answered. Met.
(iv) Continuous presence — telemetry shows 19 thinned points parked on JURONG GATEWAY ROAD from 18:22:00 through 18:27:55, speed 0.3–2.6 km/h, all within ~40 m of the pickup point (no GPS gap that leaves presence unproven). Met.

All four hold → the $5.00 fee stands (NS-1; O1 §2.1–§2.3; A3). The rider's assertion that she came out "a minute after" is contradicted by the system records: the driver was on station for 6 minutes after pressing arrival and messaged and called before cancelling, so her statement does not defeat the fee. Fee upheld = no_action; amount null (no refund).

TH: no-show/cancellation is system-final at $5.00 (TH-2), and the amount is under $10 (TH-1), so no escalation is needed. No fraud flag and no repeat no-show pattern for this rider (0 disputes in 90 days), so no flag_account; the driver's 1 dispute in 90 days was not upheld against him, so RD-6/NS-9 are inapplicable.

element_findings.element: NS-1(i) driver arrived at pickup within 200 m ("I'm Here"/auto-arrival + GPS)
element_findings.reason: GPS point ~37 m from pickup (1.33218,103.74155), within the 200 m radius; arrival event recorded.

element_findings.element: NS-1(ii) 5-minute free wait elapsed before cancellation
element_findings.reason: 6 min 0 s from arrival to cancellation, exceeding the 5-minute free wait; no record-specific no_show_threshold applies.

element_findings.element: NS-1(iii) ≥1 in-app message AND ≥1 in-app call before cancelling
element_findings.reason: Driver sent one in-app message and placed one in-app call (unanswered is still a call attempt) before cancelling at 18:27:55.

element_findings.element: NS-1(iv) driver remained at pickup throughout the wait
basis: gps 18:22:00–18:27:55 all on Jurong Gateway Road, speed <=2.6 km/h
element_findings.reason: All sampled positions are stationary within ~40 m of the pickup, no gap leaving presence unproven.

element_findings.element: NS-0 basis: reason the driver cancelled
element_findings.reason: Driver's own statement gives rider no-show as the cancellation reason, so NS-1/NS-2 govern rather than NS-3.

element_findings.element: Rider claim: cancelled about a minute before she came out
element_findings.reason: System records show 6 minutes elapsed between arrival and cancellation, contradicting the complaint; system records override statements.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider says she came out a minute after cancellation and was charged for nothing, but the arrival event (18:21:55) and cancellation (18:27:55) show the full free wait plus one extra minute elapsed, with a message and a call made to her first; NS-1 is satisfied and the $5.00 fee stands.
